memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Even if someone is not redeemed in any of these ways, they and their
children are to be released in the Year of Jubilee, for the Israelites belong
to me as servants. They are my servants, whom I brought out of Egypt. I am
the LORD your God'" - Lev 25:54-55 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends where it must. Even if no relative came, even if the person
never prospered enough to redeem himself, even if every other avenue closed —
the Jubilee would still release him. Freedom was guaranteed, because the
people belonged to God. I am the LORD your God — the same words that opened
His covenant with them close this chapter.

Notice the foundation of it all: the Israelites belong to me. Their ultimate
freedom did not rest on their circumstances, their family, or their success.
It rested on the fact that they were God's. His ownership was their
guarantee.

Dear friend, this is where all our security finally rests too. Not in our
ability to fix our situation, not in others coming through for us, but in the
fact that we belong to God. Jesus said His sheep are His, and no one can
snatch them out of His hand (John 10:28-29). Paul asks who can separate us
from the love of Christ, and answers: nothing in all creation (Rom 8:38-39).

The Jubilee reaches its true fulfilment in Christ. He has proclaimed the
year of the Lord's favour (Luke 4:19). One day the trumpet will sound, the
dead will be raised, and every child of God will go free forever (1 Cor
15:52).

Whatever holds you now, the final word belongs to your Redeemer. You are His,
and He is bringing you home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where does my ultimate security rest?
2. What holds me now that the great Jubilee will one day break?
3. How does belonging to God change the way I face my present struggles?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, my freedom rests not on my circumstances but on the fact that I
belong to You. Thank You that the final word is Yours, and You are bringing
me home. Amen.
